summary: A Readymag page for Zaatar, a slanted Arabic display face (Ruq'ah + Nastaliq with a geometric touch) by Boharat and Hey Porter!: a word slideshow and facts panel, then Egyptian colloquial sayings set huge beside vintage film stills, the alphabet in all contextual forms, five stylistic sets as before/after pairs and a wall of ligatures, all as images on black with one green accent.

instances.look: Fixed 70px black bar on every screen: Boharat calligraphic logo in an outlined oval top-left, 'TYPEFACES BLOG ABOUT SHOP' in ~11px white caps top-right (doubled in screen 10 where the stitched captures overlap)

instances.variantDefinition: An auto-advancing slideshow of pre-set display compositions (a place name, the family name in each weight with labels, a short phrase) in a full-width banner, one word or lockup per slide, usually above a facts panel; the hero is a sequence of words rather than one wordmark
instances.look: A charcoal banner across the top of the page with one huge light-grey Arabic word per slide: 'القاهرة' (Cairo) in the capture; other slides show 'زعتر' three times with green oval stamps 'ZAATAR BLACK' / 'ZAATAR REGULAR', and 'لحظة نحن هنا؟' in white over green
instances.ux: Slides cross-fade/slide automatically (13 slides, '3 / 13' counter in the DOM); no visible controls; nav fixed above
instances.learn: Rotate a few words with local meaning (a city, the name in each weight with a stamp label) instead of one fixed wordmark: the first screen shows range and place in a few seconds

reconstruction.layout: Banner full-bleed 1440×506px starting under the 66px nav, background #2d2d2d; one composition centred per slide, word ~640×320px; slides are 4267×1500 images scaled to fit
reconstruction.typography: Zaatar Black/Regular as images, light grey #d4d4d4, word cap height ~250px; badge labels in a small Latin serif inside rotated green ovals
reconstruction.behaviour: Readymag widget-slideshow, autoplay, transitions between 13 images; no arrows shown
reconstruction.content: Place name (Cairo), the family name per weight with stamps, a colloquial phrase

instances.look: Under the banner, a black facts strip: two narrow spec columns ('Display - 3 Style', 'Regular, Bold, and Black', 'Release October 2021', 'Version 0.3', a 'Specimen' file link, 'In progress/available', 'Designers' Tawfiq Dawi and Abdo Mohamed with → arrows) and a wide column of two small paragraphs
instances.ux: Designer names link out with arrows; 'Specimen' opens a PDF on Google Drive
instances.learn: Pair the origin story with a compact spec card (styles, release, version, status, designers) so the facts are scannable beside the prose

reconstruction.layout: Strip ~330px tall on #0e0e0e; columns at x≈116 (180px), x≈386 (180px) and x≈626 (~620px text); rows ~26px apart, small icons before 'Specimen' and 'In progress'
reconstruction.typography: Labels ~12px Graphik Medium white, values ~12px Regular; paragraph ~12px Regular, leading ~1.5, white
reconstruction.content: Real copy: 'Zaatar is a dynamic Arabic typeface abstracted from a mixture of Arabic Ruq'ah and Nastaliq, the slanted baseline…'; 'Zaatar means thyme… first collaboration between Boharat (Cairo) and Hey Porter! (Jordan)'
reconstruction.assets: Small file and list icons, arrow icons

instances.look: Row of four outlined white pills under the nav, '★ In use', '✓ Opentype features', 'Glyphs', 'supported languages' (~13px), each an anchor link that scrolls the page to that section

On black, Egyptian colloquial sayings set huge in light grey and centred ('القاهرة', 'أكل العيش صعب ومرّ' twice, 'مساكين بنضحك من البلوة', 'الصبر' in a 2×2 pair, 'حكي كلونيا حكي جاتوه'), each paired with a small vintage film still (a Cairo alley, an oud player, two actors laughing) tucked behind or beside the words
instances.ux: Plain scroll; a green four-way arrow icon between the 'الصبر' pairs and tiny green 'M' / 'E' marks around 'حكي' are decorative
instances.learn: Use well-known film lines and sayings of the target culture as specimen copy, with a still from the source: local readers recognise the words before they judge the letters

reconstruction.layout: ~3600px of black, single centred column ~900px; each saying 1–3 lines with line height ~0.9 of the type size; film stills ~350×500px (or ~420×290) overlapping the left edge of the words; generous ~200px gaps between sayings; repeated lines stacked to show rhythm

reconstruction.behaviour: none (static images; Readymag fade-in on some widgets)
reconstruction.content: Egyptian colloquial sayings and film quotes: 'earning a living is hard and bitter', 'poor us, we laugh at our misfortune', 'patience'

instances.look: Two rows of numerals in green, Arabic-Indic '١٢٣٤٥٦٧٨٩٠' above Western '1234567890', a thin green rule, then the whole Arabic alphabet in light grey running right-to-left as lines, every letter followed by its contextual forms (ب ببب ت تتت …), ending with punctuation and both numeral sets
instances.learn: For Arabic, list each letter with its initial, medial and final forms joined in a row: the set reads as connected script, not isolated glyphs

instances.look: Five rows, each a word twice side by side (default left, with the stylistic set right: 'مصر', 'الطرف', 'اللعبي', 'مساحة', …), a small green dot under the changed letter of the right-hand word and a green label 'STYLISTEC SET 01…05' at the right edge
instances.learn: Mark the one changed glyph with a small coloured dot under the 'after' word: the eye finds the alternate instantly without arrows or outlines
